slots.practicalActivity: Open a blank workbook and drill the shortcuts covered (Ctrl+Arrow, Ctrl+Shift+Arrow, Ctrl+1, F2, Ctrl+;) against a small pasted dataset, then deliberately format the same column of numbers as General, Currency, Percentage, and Text to see how the underlying value differs from its display.
slots.deliverable: A worksheet with one column shown under four different number formats, plus a written note on which shortcuts you could reliably use without looking at the ribbon by the end.

slots.practicalActivity: Convert a raw range of at least 30 rows of sample sales data into an Excel Table with Ctrl+T, rename it from the default Table1, then create two named ranges (one for a single cell like a tax rate, one for a column) and reference both a structured Table column and a named range in formulas on the same sheet.
slots.deliverable: One named Excel Table with a formula using structured references (e.g. Table[Sales]), plus one formula referencing a named range instead of a bare cell address.

slots.practicalActivity: On your Table from Lesson 3, write a VLOOKUP that pulls a price from a second lookup table, rewrite the same lookup as an XLOOKUP, then rewrite it a third time as INDEX/MATCH, confirming all three return the same value.
slots.deliverable: Three formulas (VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH) solving the identical lookup against the same two tables, with matching results side by side.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a two-key lookup (e.g. matching on both Product and Region using INDEX/MATCH with a concatenated or array match condition), then deliberately look up a value you know doesn't exist in the source table and wrap the formula in IFERROR to return a friendly 'Not Found' instead of #N/A.
slots.deliverable: One combined multi-key lookup formula and one IFERROR-wrapped lookup that gracefully handles a guaranteed-missing value.

slots.practicalActivity: Timed drill: without looking back at the lessons, build five original lookup formulas against a dataset you set up yourself — two VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, two INDEX/MATCH, and one IFERROR-wrapped lookup against a value that doesn't exist — using table and column names of your own choosing.
slots.deliverable: Five original lookup formulas in one worksheet, each validated against a manually checked expected result.

slots.practicalActivity: On your sales Table, write a SUMIFS that totals Sales for one Region and one Category at the same time, a COUNTIFS counting orders above a threshold, an AVERAGEIFS for average order value in one Segment, and a nested IF that classifies each order into three tiers by Sales amount.
slots.deliverable: A worksheet with one SUMIFS, one COUNTIFS, one AVERAGEIFS, and one nested IF formula, each validated against a manually spot-checked row.

slots.practicalActivity: Rebuild your Lesson 10 nested IF as a flatter IFS formula, add an AND/OR condition that flags orders meeting two criteria at once, then write a date function (e.g. DATEDIF or EDATE to compute days since order) and a text function (e.g. LEFT, TRIM, or TEXTJOIN) against your data.
slots.deliverable: An IFS formula replacing the earlier nested IF, one AND/OR-based flag, and one working date function plus one working text function.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a PivotTable from your Excel Table (not a raw range), dragging one field into Rows, one into Columns, and a numeric field into Values, then add 5 new rows to the source Table and refresh the PivotTable to confirm they're picked up automatically; finally, add a PivotTable calculated field (e.g. a profit margin %) that isn't a plain column in the source data.
slots.deliverable: A PivotTable built from a Table that correctly reflects 5 newly added source rows after a refresh, plus one working PivotTable calculated field.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Slicer for a categorical field and a Timeline for a date field to your PivotTable, confirm both filter the report when clicked, then insert a PivotChart from the same PivotTable and connect the same Slicer and Timeline to it so both the table and chart update together.
slots.deliverable: One PivotTable and one PivotChart sharing a connected Slicer and Timeline, both updating together when either control is used.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, build one original PivotTable + PivotChart report from your sales Table answering a question you write yourself (e.g. 'which Region's profit margin is most volatile month to month'), including at least one calculated field and one connected Slicer or Timeline.
slots.deliverable: One original PivotTable/PivotChart pair with a self-written business question, a calculated field, and a connected filter control, all demonstrated working together.

slots.practicalActivity: Enter =SEQUENCE(10) in an empty cell and confirm it spills automatically, then on your sales Table write a FILTER formula returning only orders above a threshold, a SORT formula ranking products by Sales descending, and a UNIQUE formula listing distinct Regions.
slots.deliverable: One SEQUENCE spill demo plus working FILTER, SORT, and UNIQUE formulas against your real sales data, each confirmed to spill correctly.

slots.practicalActivity: Click into the middle of one of your spilled FILTER/SORT/UNIQUE ranges to confirm the formula bar shows it dimmed and uneditable, then refactor your most complex formula from this chapter using LET to name its intermediate values and avoid repeating the same sub-expression twice.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed spilled-range behavior check, plus one formula refactored with LET that produces the identical result to its original version.

slots.practicalActivity: Export a copy of your sales data to CSV, load it via Data > Get Data > From Text/CSV into the Power Query Editor, remove one junk column, fix at least two data types, and remove blank rows, watching each action appear as a new step in Applied Steps.
slots.deliverable: A Power Query with a visible Applied Steps list showing at minimum a Removed Columns, a Changed Type, and a Removed Rows (blanks) step, loaded back into the workbook.

slots.practicalActivity: Split your sales data into two mock month-range CSV exports, load each as its own query, then use Append Queries to stack them back into one combined table, and separately Merge in a small Region-to-Manager lookup table as a new column.
slots.deliverable: One appended combined query stacking two source files, and one merged query with a new column pulled from a separate lookup table.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, take a messy exported CSV (introduce a stray column, a few blank rows, and one inconsistent date format yourself) and build a Power Query from scratch that cleans it end to end in at least five chained steps before loading it to a worksheet.
slots.deliverable: One original Power Query with five or more chained cleaning steps, loaded into the workbook, built from a dataset you deliberately made messy yourself.

slots.practicalActivity: For three questions you write yourself (a comparison, a trend over time, and a distribution), pick the right chart family and build each one using Insert > Recommended Charts as a starting point, then set up a Goal Seek run that solves for the unit price needed to hit a revenue target you choose.
slots.deliverable: Three charts, each matched to a self-written question and chart family, plus one working Goal Seek run (Set cell, To value, By changing cell) that lands on your chosen target.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one capstone analyst workbook from your cleaned sales data, pulling together the whole course: a Power Query-cleaned source table, at least two lookup formulas (XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH), two SUMIFS/COUNTIFS-style aggregations, one PivotTable with a connected Slicer, one dynamic array formula (FILTER, SORT, or UNIQUE), and one chart choosing the right type for its question.
slots.deliverable: A single finished workbook combining Power Query, lookups, aggregation formulas, a PivotTable with a Slicer, a dynamic array formula, and a chart, suitable to show as a portfolio piece demonstrating the full course.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can clean and reshape raw exports with Power Query, build reliable lookup and aggregation formulas (XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, SUMIFS/COUNTIFS), summarize data with PivotTables and PivotCharts, use modern dynamic array functions, and build a chart or Goal Seek scenario that directly answers a real business question.
